Messengers, bring one who turns away from the eleventh-day vow, of fierce character, fond of slandering people and reviling others, destroyer of villages, filled with the worst hostility, greedy for the wealth of Brahmins.
naradapuran:22:82	Bring by force those very foolish men, deep in sin, who turn from devotion to Vishnu, who do not bow to Narayana, protector of those who seek refuge, and who do not go to Vishnu's temple.
When I heard what Yama thus declared there, burned with remorse, I recalled my own censured deeds.
By remorse for evil deeds and by hearing of true dharma, all my sins vanished there without remainder.
Freed of all remnant of sin, I attained likeness to Hari, shining like a thousand suns, and Yama bowed to me.
Seeing this, Yama's messengers, astonished and overcome with awe, placed supreme faith in what Yama had said.
Then Yama honoured me and at once sent me on a vimana, amid hundreds of aerial cars, to Vishnu's supreme abode.
With ten million aerial cars equipped with every enjoyment, by that act I lived in Vishnu's world, O sage.
Having stayed in Vishnu's abode for a thousand crores of kalpas and a hundred crores of kalpas, I afterwards went to Indra's world.
There too, rich in all enjoyments and honoured by all the gods, I stayed in heaven for as long, and then came to earth.
Here too I was born in your family of Vishnu's devotees; because I remember my past lives, I know all this, O lord of sages.
Therefore I undertake worship of Vishnu with the boys; I did not know before that this was the eleventh-day vow.
By the power of remembering my births, I now know it. Here, too, the fruit of what I did myself is this.
What then of those who keep the eleventh-day vow with devotion, O lord? Therefore I shall keep the auspicious eleventh-day vow, O best of Brahmins,
and daily worship of Vishnu, desiring the highest place. Those men who keep the eleventh-day vow with faith
gain Vishnu's abode, which gives supreme bliss." Hearing his son's words, the sage Galava was delighted,
and attained supreme satisfaction, very joyful in mind: "My birth has become fruitful; my family is purified,
since you were born in my house, devoted to Vishnu." Thus, satisfied in mind by his son's deed,
he duly taught him the method of worshipping Hari. Thus, O best of sages, I have told you this as it was, in brief and in detail; what else do you wish to hear?
He should approach his own wives in their fertile season; he should wish the good of all people, be auspicious and speak kindly;
free of strain, joyful in mind, patient, not overly proud — this is the common duty of all classes, declared by the sages.
All attain the state of a sage by the duties proper to their own order of life. In distress a Brahmin may resort to the Kshatriya's conduct, O Brahmin;
a Kshatriya in great distress may resort to the Vaishya's livelihood; but a twice-born man should not resort to the Shudra's livelihood even in the greatest distress.
If a foolish twice-born takes it up, he goes to the state of an outcaste. For the three — Brahmin, Kshatriya and Vaishya — O best of sages,
four orders of life are taught; a fifth is not allowed: the student, the householder, the forest-dweller, and the mendicant.
Through these four orders the highest dharma is accomplished; Vishnu is pleased, O Brahmin, with one devoted to the yoga of action.
Of one free of desire, with a peaceful mind and devoted to his own duty, then he goes to the highest place from which he does not return.
The staff of a Vaishya is of goat's-wood (or "aja"); I shall tell the staffs in order: the Brahmin's is of palasha, the king's of udumbara,
the Vaishya's of bilva; hear their measure from me. The Brahmin's staff reaches the hair, the king's the forehead,
and the wise say the Vaishya's reaches the tip of the nose. Now I shall tell the garments of Brahmins and the rest in order:
ochre, madder-red and turmeric-yellow are declared. The twice-born, invested with the sacred thread, a Brahmin, devoted to serving his teacher,
should live in his teacher's house until he has learned the Veda; the student should bathe in the morning,
and fetch fuel, kusha grass, fruit and the like for his teacher every day, O lord of sages. The sacred thread, deerskin and staff,
if lost or broken, should be replaced with a mantra, and the old one cast in water. His livelihood, they say, is only alms-food.
With self-controlled senses he should bring alms from the house of a Vedic scholar. The word "bhavat" comes first for a Brahmin, in the middle for a king,
and last for a Vaishya, in the words of asking alms. Morning and evening he should attend the fire according to custom, with senses controlled.
The student should do daily the Brahma-sacrifice (study) and tarpana. One who abandons the fire-rite is called fallen by the wise,
and one without the Brahma-sacrifice is called a Brahmin-slayer. He should worship the gods and serve his teacher step by step.
He should feed on alms-food always, never eating the food of one house alone; having brought alms from the houses of blameless Brahmins, with senses controlled,
he should offer it to the teacher and eat in silence with his leave. He should avoid honey, women, meat, salt, betel and tooth-twigs,
eating leftovers and sleeping by day; umbrella, sandals, perfumes, garlands and ointments;
water-sports, dancing, singing and instrumental music; he should avoid slander, anger, idle talk and eye-ointment;
he should avoid contact with heretics and the company of Shudras. He should be given to saluting his elders in order.
Elders are three: in knowledge, in austerity, and in age. The teacher who removes the sorrows of the spirit and the rest
by teaching the Veda and scriptures should be saluted first. In saluting, the twice-born says "I am so-and-so."
A Brahmin should never salute Kshatriyas and the like; nor an unbeliever, one who breaks the limits, the ungrateful, or a village priest;
a thief or a gambler should never be saluted; a heretic, an outcast, one lapsed from the thread, or one living by the military profession;
a sinner of great sins should never be saluted; a madman, a rogue, a cheat, one who is running, or one who is impure;
one with oiled head or one muttering prayers should not be saluted; a quarrelsome man, one vomiting, or one in the middle of water;
one carrying alms-food or sleeping should not be saluted. A murderer of her husband, a menstruating woman, a woman with a paramour, a woman in childbed, one who has miscarried,
an ungrateful or fierce woman should never be saluted. In an assembly, in a sacrificial hall, or in temples,
a salutation to each individually takes away the merit earlier acquired. One performing shraddha, a vow, a gift, worship of gods,
a sacrifice or tarpana should not be saluted. One who, when saluted, does not return the salutation
should not be saluted — he is to be treated as a Shudra. Having washed his feet and sipped water, facing the teacher always,
the wise student should clasp his feet and study. On the eighth days, the fourteenth, the first and parvan days,
at the Mahabharani star, on Shravana-dvadashi, in the dark half of Bhadrapada on the second day,
on the seventh of the bright half of Magha, on the ninth of Ashvina, when the sun has a halo, when a Vedic scholar has come to the house,
when a Brahmin is bound, when a quarrel has grown, at twilight, when thunder roars, when unseasonal rain falls,
at the fall of meteors and thunderbolts, when a Brahmin is insulted, on the Manvantara beginnings and the four Yuga beginnings, O divine sage,
no twice-born who desires the fruit of all rites should study. The third of the bright half of Vaishakha, the thirteenth of the dark half of Bhadrapada,
the pure ninth of Kartika, the fifteenth of Magha — these are declared the beginnings of ages, making gifts imperishable.
I shall tell the Manvantara beginnings; hear with attention: the bright ninth of Ashvina, the bright twelfth of Kartika,
the third of Chaitra and of Bhadrapada, the bright tenth of Ashadha, the bright seventh of Magha,
the dark eighth of Shravana and the full moon of Ashadha, the new moon of Phalguna, the bright eleventh of Pausha,
the full moons of Kartika, Phalguna, Chaitra and Jyeshtha — these are called Manvantara beginnings, making gifts imperishable.
Brahmins should perform shraddha on the Manvantara and Yuga beginnings. When invited to a shraddha, at eclipses of the moon and sun,
at the two solstices, at an earthquake, O sage, when the throat is sore, on a gloomy day, one should never study.
On all these study-forbidden days, O Narada, for foolish students who study then, Yama himself cuts off progeny, wisdom, fame and wealth,
longevity, strength and health. One who studies on a forbidden day should be known as a slayer of Brahmins.
One should not speak with him nor live with him. Some say the initiation of those born to adulteresses (kunda, golaka) and the dull and their sons...
One who, not having studied the Veda, takes pains elsewhere
is to be regarded as equal to a Shudra, a favourite guest of hell. A Brahmin without Vedic learning who takes up the conduct (of a Brahmin)
does not gain the fruit of conduct, just like a Shudra. Daily, occasional, desire-motivated and any other Vedic rite
of an unlearned Brahmin is all fruitless. Vishnu is made of the Word-Brahman; the Veda is Hari himself.
Therefore a Brahmin who studies the Veda obtains all desires.
